applied.title: Co-op mirror never restores the flat idle for a directional-walk boss
applied.summary: The 09-03 mirror port copied the live path's directional branch but dropped its `or _cur_dir != ""` restore, so a boss with a DIRECTIONAL walk and a FLAT idle (empty _strip_walk, empty _dir_idle) never swapped back when it stopped on a guest: the mirror kept the last walk strip and cycled it standing still. The mirror's non-directional arm is now the same shape as the live path -- `want_walk := net_walk and not _strip_walk.is_empty()`, restore on the walk-state flip OR whenever we are arriving from the directional path, clearing the `_cur_dir` latch so a later walk re-picks. Same guard chain as the live path, so a body with no idle strip at all still cannot reach it.
applied.test: Co-op: host a session, guest joins, fight any of the 18 BOSS_DIRECTIONAL_WALK bosses (vargoth, korrag, nullwarden, ...) and watch it on the GUEST screen when it stops moving -- it should return to its flat breathing idle instead of marching in place.
applied.risk: The branch now runs `_apply_strip(_strip_idle)` once on the first mirror frame for bodies whose `_cur_dir` still holds its "s" default -- a one-time redundant re-apply of the strip already up, identical to what the live path does.

applied.title: _lean low-pass had no is_finite guard -- one bad frame latched sprite.rotation = NaN forever
applied.summary: `_lean` is an exponential low-pass exactly like `_face_vx`, but only `_face_vx` was guarded; `lerpf(NaN, x, t)` stays NaN for the life of the node, so a single non-finite `velocity.x` permanently wrote `sprite.rotation = NaN` and the _physics_process NaN scrub could not un-poison it. Both the target and the accumulator are now clamped to 0.0 when non-finite, so a body that already latched recovers as soon as the sim does. The mirror path reached this without any sim bug at all, since its `velocity` is derived from a possibly non-finite `net_target`.
applied.test: Force a mob's velocity.x to NAN for one frame from the dev panel (or spawn one at a (nan,nan) position and let the scrub repair it) and confirm the body renders upright afterwards instead of disappearing.
applied.risk: None -- both guards are no-ops on finite values, so the normal render path is bit-identical.

applied.title: Mirror stride clock ignored the host's speed ratio -- slowed and wandering mobs skated on a guest
applied.summary: The 09-03 stride/ground coupling multiplies the walk clock by the live speed ratio on the host, but the mirror tick applied only the cruise multiplier and the gait personality, so on a guest every slowed, hazard-iced, frenzied or half-pace-wandering mob still played its walk at cruise. The mirror now measures the ground speed it actually RENDERS -- its own per-frame displacement, low-passed at the new Balance.MOB_NET_STRIDE_EASE because a 20 Hz snapshot stream makes the raw step lumpy -- and feeds that through the same clampf(spd/speed, STRIDE_RATE_MIN, STRIDE_RATE_MAX) band. Deliberately NOT the existing presentation `velocity`, which is the un-damped lerp residual over delta and reads several times cruise.
applied.test: Co-op: on the guest, chill/slow a mob (Killing Frost, ice hazard) or watch an unaggroed wanderer at half pace -- its legs should match its ground speed instead of running at cruise.
applied.risk: The low-pass starts at 0, so a freshly spawned mirror walks its legs at STRIDE_RATE_MIN for roughly the first half second; packet loss that stalls net_target also slows the legs, which matches the body actually standing still. One new tuning constant lands in balance.gd (mobile picks it up on the next sync).

applied.title: Death reset missed pounce_time and the boss tell pose
applied.summary: _play_death_anim cleared the transient pose channels it knew about but not `pounce_time`, which is only decremented in _tick_traits -- and _physics_process skips that entirely once `dying` -- while _render_tail reads it unconditionally, so a mob killed inside its 0.30 s lunge held the stretch and the pinned bank for its whole death clip and fade. The same reset never touched the boss telegraph channels, whose tween outlives the AI, so a boss killed inside a fuse rose/coiled/leaned through its own death. Death now zeroes pounce_time and calls a new virtual `_end_tell()`; Boss overrides it to kill the driving `_tell_tw` before delegating, since that tween lives in the derived layer.
applied.test: Kill a pouncing mob (wolf/lunger) mid-leap and a boss during a visible windup fuse; both should collapse or play their death clip at neutral pose instead of stretched-and-banked or still rising.
applied.risk: Boss._end_tell is a new derived-layer override calling super() -- the only new cross-file change, and calls still flow derived to base. Nothing else calls _end_tell, so no live telegraph is cut short.

applied.title: Elite promotion rescaled the body but not the HP bar, ground AO or contact shadow
applied.summary: _rescale_body recomputed only _scale_base/sprite.scale, while the HP bar's head line, the ground-AO disc and the contact shadow were all derived once in make() from the pre-promotion vscale -- so an elite's head line rose about 50% (ELITE_SIZE_BIAS x ELITE_SPRITE_MULT) while its bar sat inside the sprite and its ground furniture stayed base-sized; _spawn_add's 0.8x weakling and swap_sprite's Saint Varo throne->standing cell had the same hole. make()'s bar-height math is now the helper `_measure_bar_y` (reading _scale_base and dropping the sprite.position.y term, both exactly the make()-time values, so spawn results are unchanged) and a new `_refresh_body_furniture` re-fits the bar, AO disc and contact ellipse. It is called at the end of _rescale_body and of swap_sprite; make() keeps references to the two ground sprites for it.
applied.test: Dev-panel spawn a mob, promote it to elite, and check the HP bar sits above the enlarged head with the AO pool and shadow under the whole body; repeat for a spawner's weakling add and for Saint Varo's 25% throne->standing swap.
applied.risk: _measure_bar_y re-decodes the strip head line on a cache miss, but _strip_head_y is cached per texture RID so a swap costs at most one decode. _refresh_body_furniture reads the CURRENT strip, so it assumes the idle/base strip is applied -- true at all three call sites.

applied.title: A guest's damage rendered as the host's own big number
applied.summary: The host resolves every hit -- its own AND every guest's -- so the big/bright 'mine' branch was taken for damage the host merely ran the math for, and the host alone could not tell his numbers from his party's (the ally fan RPC bails on the server, so nothing corrected it). Ownership now decides the style: `stat_credit` (the source captured before the reflect fallback, so hazard and DoT ticks still read as yours) is checked with `is_locally_controlled()`, and a non-local striker draws the small dim `spawn_ally_damage` number instead. is_locally_controlled() is always true offline, so solo is untouched, and the outgoing host_fan_damage call is unchanged.
applied.test: Co-op: host and guest both hit the same enemy; on the HOST screen the guest's numbers should be the small cool-tinted ally style and only the host's own should be big. Solo: numbers must be unchanged (quick suite covers the solo damage path).
applied.risk: Uses stat_credit rather than the post-fallback `striker` the fan uses, so a hit with no recorded source stays big/local -- the current behaviour. If a future path forgets to set hit_src for a guest blow, that blow would render as the host's own again.

applied.title: Cast theme payload survives the windup await (per-cast snapshot/restore)
applied.summary: use_ability stamps the cast's theme package into shared instance state (_tfx/_tcolor/_themed/_cast_base), but every kit basic awaits a 0.10-0.25 s windup and only reads it on resume, so a second ability pressed inside that window made the first cast land on the SECOND ability's riders (splash/dot/pierce/echo/slow/stun_chance/vuln/brittle/twin plus the flat cast base), not just its tint. Added player_combat.cast_wait(sec) -- the one cast-windup wait, which snapshots the payload before the timer and restores it on resume -- and routed all 11 kit windup awaits through it (archer x3, assassin x2, mage, paladin x2, warlock x2, warrior). player.gd's stamp site now documents the contract so anything added to the payload gets restored too.
applied.lines: player.gd 826-835 (comment); player_combat.gd 963-982 (new cast_wait); player_kit_archer.gd 29,57,206; player_kit_assassin.gd 28,126; player_kit_mage.gd 22; player_kit_paladin.gd 67,265; player_kit_warlock.gd 26,260; player_kit_warrior.gd 42
applied.test: Equip themes with clearly different riders on a1 and a2 of one class (e.g. warrior), press a1 then a2 within ~0.1 s, and check the a1 cleave still applies a1's rider (spawn_text/dot tick or a printed effects dict at hit_enemy). An autotest addition would stamp _tfx, call use_ability("a1"), overwrite _tfx from a second use_ability, wall-clock await past the windup and assert the landed effects match the first cast.
applied.risk: Cross-file: the fix cannot live in player.gd alone -- GDScript has no per-coroutine state, so the restore must happen where the cast resumes (the kit's await). Each call-site edit is a mechanical one-liner, same duration expression, same frame. Side effect: after two overlapping casts the shared payload now holds the LAST-RESUMED cast's package instead of the last-STAMPED one; projectiles already snapshot p.fx at spawn and hit_enemy only merges _tfx keys the caller did not pass, so this is a strict improvement, but a very late un-snapshotted hit merges a different (correcter) package than before. Three long non-windup awaits were deliberately left alone as out of scope: assassin ult 0.16 s execution loop and 5 s x_mark cleanup, warlock soul-rip 0.22 s pull ticks (that one already carries its own fx_copy).

applied.title: Fire-on-move walk no longer inherits the archer's due-south bow bias
applied.summary: The archer's standing bow clips bias a due-south aim onto the SE/SW sprite (the flat south pose holds the bow across her body), but that hint was set before the walk_fire block rewrites action_clip to attack_walk, and only cleared after play_action had already consumed it. The attack_walk one-shot therefore locked 45 degrees off the aim on any due-south shot -- even while travelling north -- despite the archer shipping a full 8-direction attack_walk set including _s. The walk_fire branch now clears action_face_hint before playing the stride, so _action_facing_vec falls back to the aim/travel line.
applied.test: As the archer, hold a movement key and spam Quick Shot with a target due south (and again while running north): the played strip should be archer_attack_walk_s (or the travel facing), not _se/_sw. Verifiable in a shot rig by printing _loco_dir/_clip at the moment play_action fires.
applied.risk: Only reachable for a moving basic on a class with an attack_walk strip; the dash hint (the other action_face_hint writer) can never be walk_fire, and the mid-cycle re-cast branch calls no play_action so clearing early is inert there. If the standing south bias was ever wanted on the walk strip too, this removes it -- but the walk set has its own _s art, which is the point.

applied.title: Co-op desktop overlay input gate now actually gates
applied.summary: game.gd zeroes the local intents every _process frame an overlay is up, but player.gd's physics frame re-polls the raw keyboard into the same fields before anything consumes them, so online (where the tree never pauses, section 5.4) a key held when a menu/dialogue/choice/chat opened kept walking and casting the hero underneath it -- the keyboard twin of the touch-HUD joystick bug, invisible solo because solo pauses. player.gd now re-applies the clear right after its own poll, and the two remaining mid-frame re-polls in this file (_move_dir at the movement read and in the ghost drift) read the frame's already-gated intent_move instead. The overlay composite moved into game_base.input_overlay_up() so game.gd and the player gate on the same one definition.
applied.test: Existing autotest _test_overlay_intent_gate still covers the shape (it passes either way headless, since no key is held). A real check: online two-client session, hold W, open the inventory -- the hero must stop. Headless, the gate can be proven by writing intent_move/intent_a1, setting hud.dialogue_active with get_tree().paused = false, awaiting two physics frames and asserting the player did not move (position delta 0), which the current section cannot see because it only asserts the fields.
applied.risk: Two small cross-file edits: one new helper on game_base (the composite it replaces was inline in game.gd, unchanged in meaning) so the base-layer player can ask without duplicating it. Replacing _move_dir() with intent_move at those two sites is behaviour-identical -- both run in the same physics frame as the poll, and the base-layer poll refresh exists for out-of-frame callers (dash_vec, game.gd), which are untouched. Real behaviour change: input is now genuinely dead under an overlay in a session, including the ghost drift; anything that relied on walking under an open menu online would stop.

applied.title: Telegraph comments claimed a shape-following hit test that does not exist
applied.summary: The SHAPE VOCABULARY comment in telegraph() claimed "the hit test below follows the same shape", and the BOSS_TELL doc in balance.gd repeated it while pointing at a non-existent function (game_base._tell_figure). The actual hit test is an unchanged full-disc radius check (pl.global_position.distance_to(pos) > radius + 8.0), exactly as _tell_accent's own header states. Both comments now say the accent is decoration drawn inside the disc, warn against "fixing" the test into a shaped one (it would silently shrink all 47 boss danger areas), and the balance.gd reference points at the real function _tell_accent. No behaviour changed.
applied.lines: game/scripts/game_base.gd:3241-3249 (comment block inside telegraph()); also game/scripts/balance.gd:161-164 (BOSS_TELL table doc)
applied.test: Compile gate run after the edit prints COMPILE OK (121 scripts). Behaviour is provably unchanged since only comment lines differ (git diff shows no statement changes); the existing autotest telegraph/_tell_accent coverage (autotest.gd:9975) continues to exercise the accent builder.
applied.risk: None to runtime: comment-only edits in two files, no code paths touched. The only residual risk is doc drift if the hit test is ever genuinely made shape-aware, in which case both comments must be updated together.

applied.title: Structure lights read the room they stand in, not the player's room
applied.summary: `_add_structure` scaled every decal torch and pure light socket by `light_mult`, the global budget `refresh_ambience` derives from `cur_room` — but scenery builds run before `cur_room` advances to the room being built, so each structure baked the PREVIOUS room's terrain budget (and the first room of a chapter kept the last room of the previous one). It now resolves the structure's own room once (`room_at_pos(pos)`) and uses the existing `_zone_light_mult()` helper for both the PointLight2D energy and the floor pools, falling back to `light_mult` only when the structure sits outside the room graph. No new tuning numbers; the two per-light `room_at_pos` calls collapse into that one lookup.
applied.test: Boot a chapter and walk from a bright terrain room into a dark one (or vice versa) that holds a torch-decal / light-socket structure and compare brazier energy against a room of the same terrain reached from a same-terrain neighbour; in code, assert `_zone_light_mult(room_at_pos(struct.position))` matches the built PointLight2D energy / 0.8 for a structure in a room other than `cur_room`.
applied.risk: Behavioural change is intentional: lit structures in a room whose terrain differs from the previous room now come up at a different energy than before (correct one). Structures placed outside any room cell keep the old global-mult path, so nothing regresses there.

applied.title: Death reset respawns a social room's promoted ELITE
applied.summary: `_reset_room_enemies` rebuilt a room only from the zone's authored pack list, so the lone miniboss a social room rolls (`_spawn_elite_room`, which is not an authored pack) was deleted by the reset sweep and never came back: dying once in an elite social room left it permanently empty and its reward unreachable. The reset now re-runs the build path's roll verbatim — fresh `_social_rng(i)`, same `Balance.ELITE_SOCIAL_ROOM_CHANCE * weekly_fx("elite")` gate, the same rng instance handed to `_spawn_elite_room` — so the same seed re-spawns the same guardian. Its only caller already guards on the room being uncleared, so a beaten elite room still stays quiet.
applied.test: Seed a run into a social room where `social_holds_elite(i)` is true, confirm the elite spawned, kill the player in that room, and after the death reset assert an Enemy with `zone_idx == i` and `elite` promotion exists and `zone_alive[i] == 1` (the same kind/level as before the death, since the rng is re-seeded from `wander_seed`).
applied.risk: If a player somehow kills the elite and then dies in that same room before `_room_cleared` marks it cleared, the guardian would respawn; the caller's `not cleared.get(death_room, false)` guard makes that window effectively the same one that already respawns killed-but-uncleared pack mobs. `_spawn_elite_room` keeps its own `net_guest()` early-out, so guests are unaffected.

applied.title: Codex bestiary misses the Moonfen boss (first_howl) because it only walks Story.CHAPTER_LIST
applied.summary: The codex derived every bestiary shelf from Story.CHAPTER_LIST alone, but the Q13 interludes register their world in Story.STANDALONE_WORLDS and are deliberately kept out of CHAPTER_LIST, so the Moonfen's final boss (first_howl) was invisible in the Bosses shelf and instead sat on the dev-only Future shelf while the player could kill it. Added one shared helper, _codex_worlds(), that merges the campaign chapters with the standalone side-chapters (chapters first, so story order is unchanged) and routed the four enemy-derivation readers through it: _used_enemy_kinds, _kind_chapters, the sort order in _bestiary_rows, and the chapter chip group. first_howl is already in menus.gd BOSS_KINDS, so it now buckets as a boss, carries 'The Moonfen' as its chapter label, sorts after the campaign, and gets its own filter chip.
applied.test: Open the codex Bosses shelf and confirm 'The First Howl' appears with the tag 'The Moonfen' at the end of the list, and that it is gone from dev Future > bosses. In a headless check: UICodex._used_enemy_kinds().has("first_howl") is true and UICodex._kind_chapters()["first_howl"] == "interlude_moonfen". autotest's existing UI smoke (open_codex bosses / future_bosses) covers the build path.
applied.risk: The helper allocates a shallow-copied dictionary per call and is now called a few times per shelf build; negligible next to the card building. Anything a standalone world places is now counted as 'used', so it also disappears from the dev Future shelf -- that is the intended two-list invariant. Only STANDALONE_WORLDS was folded in; endgame arenas stay out (their spawns come from the endgame controller, not zone tables).

applied.title: 'Folk of the Vale' omitted all 31 social-room wanderers
applied.summary: _npc_entries built the cast only from the zones' authored `npcs` arrays, but social rooms roll their occupant from the per-chapter wanderer pool (game_world._spawn_wanderer via Story.wanderers_for), so all 31 of those faces -- quest givers included -- were absent from the codex. Factored the per-npc dedup/role/name logic out of the zone loop into _add_npc_entry and called it a second time per chapter over Story.wanderers_for(chid), so wanderers fold into the same sprite-deduped cast and can still upgrade an existing face's quest-giver line. Their 'first met' location is the new WANDER_WHERE string, since the roll picks a fresh room each run and no single zone name is true for them.
applied.test: Open the codex Folk shelf and check for entries such as Old Digger Haim (ch3) and Tinker Osla (ch1), with detail reading 'First met in a quiet room on the road.'; toggle the 'Quest givers' chip to confirm wanderer givers are flagged. Headless: UICodex._npc_entries().size() should rise by the number of new sprites, and every Story.wanderers_for(chid) sprite should be present. autotest's open_codex("npcs") smoke covers the build.
applied.risk: The Folk shelf grows by up to 31 rows and the ledger is chunk-built, so no load spike is expected. Chapters without their own pool fall back to the Chapter 1 pool, so those six are attributed to ch1 (the first chapter that can spawn them) and the duplicates dedup away. A wanderer sprite that collides with an authored zone npc keeps the zone entry, as before. No autotest asserts an NPC count, so nothing should break.

applied.title: Crystal Archmage twin Firebolt leaks a floating cast focus (and can index out of range) when twin/skin changes across the windup await
applied.summary: Mage Firebolt spawned its Crystal Archmage cast focuses from the pre-windup twin/skin state but consumed them from the state read after the cast await, so a swap across that window either stranded a focus in the world forever (unlike the Void Weaver eye it has no timer fuse, and its aura tween is set_loops()) or indexed crystal_focuses[1] on a one-element array. Release now reconciles the focus array against the release-time twin/skin read instead of snapshotting it: extra focuses are dismissed through the normal fade path, and a missing one is appended as null, which _cast_crystal_focus_bolt already handles by spawning on demand. Release-time behavior and targeting are unchanged for both the base spell and the skin.
applied.lines: game/scripts/player_kit_mage.gd:30-42 (insert only; no other file touched)
applied.test: Headless: play the mage as skin crystal_archmage, call _use_mage("a1", 1.0), and mutate _tfx["twin"] (0->1 and 1->0) during the cast_wait window; after a wall-clock await, assert get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("crystal_archmage_cast_focus").is_empty() and that no index error was raised. qa_skins.gd:208 already uses that exact group-survivor check for the non-swap case.
applied.risk: Low. The only behavioral change is in the previously-broken mismatch window; in the normal case needed_focuses equals the spawned count and both while loops are no-ops. Worst case in the swap window is one visually cheaper bolt (a focus spawned at release with duration 0.0 rather than a fully formed prelude), which is the same fallback the code already used for an invalidated focus.

applied.title: Archer windup now routes through swing_delay() so the loose tracks fit_action_clip's haste
applied.summary: The archer was the only kit awaiting Balance.ARCHER_LOOSE_DELAY raw; the other five route their windup through swing_delay(), whose final `return base / _clip_haste` is what pulls a cast's contact time in when fit_action_clip re-paces the clip. Quick Shot's fire-on-move path calls fit_action_clip(cds["a1"]) on every moving cast, so at high cdr the sped-up draw-release frame passed well before the fixed 0.25 s wait expired and the arrow left after the cycle had ended. All three archer windups (Quick Shot, Arrow Storm, Multishot) now wait swing_delay(Balance.ARCHER_LOOSE_DELAY).
applied.test: Compile gate green (COMPILE OK, 121 scripts). Behavioural check mirrors autotest's existing assassin case (autotest.gd ~4490): set game.player._strike_clip = "attack" and _clip_haste = 1.5, assert game.player.swing_delay(Balance.ARCHER_LOOSE_DELAY) == Balance.ARCHER_LOOSE_DELAY / 1.5 and 1.0 returns the raw value. In-game: archer with heavy cdr, hold a movement key and spam Quick Shot — the arrow should leave on the string-snap frame of the walk-fire stride, not after it resets.
applied.risk: Behaviour changes only where _clip_haste != 1.0 — i.e. the fire-on-move Quick Shot under a short cooldown; the arrow now leaves proportionally earlier (never later, since fit_action_clip is speed-up only and capped by ACTION_CLIP_MAX_HASTE). Skins.SWING has no archer entries and the archer has no "attackb" clip, so swing_delay's skin/alt-swing branches are inert here and standing casts, Multishot and the ult are numerically unchanged. Balance side effect: a spammed moving Quick Shot resolves its damage slightly sooner at endgame cdr.

applied.title: Weekly-challenge claim ledger is never saved (Renown is), so the weekly reward is re-farmable
applied.summary: The weekly completion claim paid Renown straight into meta.json (persisted immediately) while its once-per-week ledger, weekly_claimed_week, lives in the character save and was never written: on the solo/host victory path _finish_weekly ran inside end_it AFTER state = ST_VICTORY, and autosave() gates on ST_PLAYING, so no later write could reach disk and a reload re-armed the same weekly reward. _finish_weekly now autosaves alongside the payout (claim_vault's precedent, inside the claim branch so it costs one write per week), and end_it grades the run and banks the weekly claim BEFORE the state switch, matching how net_victory already banks a guest's credit while still ST_PLAYING. No behaviour change for a run that is not the weekly, and no tuning numbers were touched.
applied.lines: 639-656 (_finish_weekly claim branch) and 1154-1172 (the end_it victory lambda)
applied.test: Existing coverage: autotest's retention section (weekly fx) and the renown section's save round-trip. To exercise the actual defect, set weekly_active = true with weekly_week = _week_index() and weekly_claimed_week = -1, drive a chapter victory, then round-trip the character save (SaveGame.write / apply as the renown section already does) and assert weekly_claimed_week == _week_index() survives, plus that a second _finish_weekly pays no Renown. Per project rules that belongs in a new section, not an edit to an existing one; nothing was added to autotest here.
applied.risk: Low. run_results() is pure, so hoisting it above the state switch changes nothing in the card; the only ordering shift is that the weekly gold/gem/Renown payout and its shout now land one step earlier, while the world is still ST_PLAYING (which is where the gem give_loot and spawn_text belong anyway). net_victory now writes twice on a fresh weekly claim (once inside _finish_weekly, once at its own trailing autosave) - harmless, at most one extra character write per week. Dedicated servers are unaffected: has_local_player() is false, so res stays {} and the weekly branch is skipped exactly as before.

applied.title: next_free_slot()/exists() ignore the .bak that read()/list() resurrect
applied.summary: SaveGame.exists() tested only the main save file while read_json() falls back to the ".bak" atomic_store leaves behind, so a slot whose main file was lost or truncated still listed and still loaded its hero, yet next_free_slot() offered that same slot to a new character and overwrote the only recoverable copy. exists() now reports occupancy the way read()/list() see it - main file OR its .bak - which fixes next_free_slot(), the dev_panel benchmark-roster scan and the game.gd new-character slot pick in one place. delete() already removes the .bak/.tmp sidecars, so a deleted slot is still free by either test.
applied.test: Autotest section 5b already covers the delete path (delete then assert not exists). A direct check: write a save to a slot, rename save_<slot>.json to save_<slot>.json.bak (leaving no main file), then assert SaveGame.list() contains the slot AND SaveGame.exists(slot) is true / next_free_slot() skips it - it fails before this change and passes after. Compile gate green (COMPILE OK, 121 scripts); no existing autotest section was edited.
applied.risk: exists() is now slightly more conservative: a slot holding only a .bak (or only a corrupt main file, as before) is treated as occupied, so in the pathological case where both files are unreadable the slot is never re-offered and the roster can read as full while list() shows fewer heroes. That is the safe direction (refuse to reuse rather than destroy a recoverable save) and matches the pre-existing behaviour for a corrupt main file. No caller depends on exists() meaning "the main path is openable": autotest 5b checks it after delete() (both files gone), dev_panel only skips forward past occupied slots, game.gd only picks a free slot.

applied.title: gait_shape() called every Act-1 directional-walk boss a 'glide' body
applied.summary: Art.gait_shape() fell through to the MOB_IDLE_ONLY_LOCOMOTION 'glide' default for the ten Act-1 bosses that BOSS_DIRECTIONAL_WALK gives a real authored 8-direction leg cycle to (vargoth, korrag, sexton, hrolgar, auroch_minotaur, rotmaw, kaethra, echo, stormmouth, nullwarden), so enemy.gd's _render_tail skipped the whole stride-locked juice block and the footfall block for them: no chest rise, no foot dust, no BOSS_STEP_SHAKE stomp, and only the reduced glider travel lean. gait_shape() now consults BOSS_DIRECTIONAL_WALK before the idle-only fallback, the same override enemy.gd's make() already applies to the strip path. To keep one source of truth rather than a parallel name list, BOSS_DIRECTIONAL_WALK's values changed from `true` to the body archetype ('biped' for the leg-walkers, 'glide' for the robed/floating set); every existing consumer only tests `.has()`, so no caller changed.
applied.test: Compile gate green (COMPILE OK, 121 scripts). Logic check: Art.gait_shape("vargoth") now returns "biped" (was "glide"), Art.gait_shape("choirmother") stays "glide", Art.gait_shape("wolf") stays "quad", Art.gait_shape("saint_varo") stays "glide" (idle-only, no directional walk). In-engine: dev_morph into vargoth or korrag and walk — the body should bob per step and kick dust; a quick assert in a new autotest hook over the three names would lock it in. DEFECT IS REAL (game/scripts/player_kit_mage.gd:17-61). Focuses are spawned off the pre-windup `skin`/`_tfx` read and consumed off the post-await read. All four mismatch cases are genuine:
- crystal + twin ON at spawn, twin OFF at release -> `crystal_focuses[1]` is never consumed.
- crystal at spawn, skin cleared at release -> the whole array is stranded (release takes the `_cast_bolt` branch).
- twin OFF at spawn, ON at release -> `crystal_focuses[1]` indexes a 1-element array (hard runtime error, and the second bolt never fires).
- no skin at spawn, crystal at release -> `crystal_focuses[0]` on an empty array.
The leak is unbounded, confirmed by reading the helpers: `_spawn_crystal_cast_focus` (line 273) gives the aura a `create_tween().set_loops()` pulse and NO fuse, and `grep crystal_archmage_cast_focus` over game/ shows no sweeper anywhere - only `_pick_crystal_focus_origin` (line 262) reading the group and `qa_skins.gd:208` counting survivors. THE FIX IS CORRECT.
- Reconcile-not-snapshot is the right shape: `needed_focuses` is computed from the SAME release-time `skin`/`_tfx` reads the consuming branches at lines 49-61 use, and there is no await between the reconcile and the consumption (the intervening ninthstar block is synchronous: uniq_counter/uniq_k/game.spawn_text), so array size and branch choice cannot diverge.
- Post-fix sizes are exactly right in all four cases: crystal+twin -> 2 (indices 0 and 1 valid), crystal solo -> 1, non-crystal -> 0 with everything dismissed.
- The null pad is safe and not a new path: `_cast_crystal_focus_bolt` line 314-315 already had `if focus == null or not is_instance_valid(focus): focus = _spawn_crystal_cast_focus(intended_dir, 0.0)`. Appending null to `Array[Node2D]` is legal in Godot 4 (ContainerTypeValidate accepts NIL for OBJECT element types). The on-demand spawn with duration 0.0 is consumed on the same frame (`crystal.frame = 7`, hidden, `queue_free`), and its form tween dies with the freed sprite - no orphan.
- `_dismiss_crystal_focus` is idempotent and null/freed-safe (null + is_instance_valid + a "dismissing" meta guard), so the trim cannot double-fade or crash, and it removes the node from the group immediately - the `qa_skins.gd:208` survivor assertion is not perturbed.
- `pop_back()` cannot underflow: the loop guard is `size() > needed_focuses` with needed >= 0.

CLAUDE.md AND GODOT 4.4 CHECKS, all pass:
- Variant inference trap: `var stranded: Node2D = crystal_focuses.pop_back()` is explicitly annotated, which is exactly what the rule demands. `var needed_focuses := 0` infers int cleanly, and `2 if _tfx.get("twin", 0) else 1` is the same Variant-condition ternary already proven at line 19.

That slot listed in the roster and loaded its hero, yet next_free_slot() (line 510) offered it to a new character, whose first autosave would rename the orphan .bak away (line 77-78 removes an existing .bak before rolling) and destroy the only recoverable copy. - game/scripts/ui/dev_panel.gd:782 `while slot <= MAX_SLOTS and SaveGame.exists(slot)` -> benchmark roster skips it too; note that loop writes with a raw FileAccess.WRITE (line 786), not atomic_store, so it would have clobbered the orphan with no backup of its own.

AUTOTEST CONTRACT INTACT: the only exists() assertion is autotest.gd:1716, `SaveGame.delete(MAX_SLOTS)` then `if SaveGame.exists(MAX_SLOTS): _fail("save delete failed")`. delete() (lines 458-463) loops `["", ".bak", ".tmp"]`, so the assert still passes - and it now actually proves sidecar cleanup instead of only the main file, which is a strictly stronger check.
